questions.summary: The radius of a normal control.

options.why: Square corners keep a strict, technical look.
options.when_to_choose: Choose this if the brand should feel sharp.

options.why: A small radius softens a corner without looking round.
options.when_to_choose: Choose this if you want a slight soften only.
trade_offs: The change is easy to miss.

options.why: Eight pixels is a soft corner that still looks like a control.
options.when_to_choose: Choose this if controls should feel soft but firm.
trade_offs: A sharp brand will look too round.

options.why: A large radius makes cards and buttons look soft.
options.when_to_choose: Choose this if the brand should feel soft.

options.label: Pill
options.why: A pill radius makes short controls fully round.
options.when_to_choose: Choose this if buttons should look like pills.

questions.summary: How larger surfaces relate to the base radius.

options.label: One radius
options.why: One radius keeps every corner the same.
options.when_to_choose: Choose this if you do not want a radius scale.

options.label: Linear
options.summary: Add a fixed amount each step.
options.why: Linear radius adds a fixed amount for each larger surface.
options.when_to_choose: Choose this if the steps should be even.
trade_offs: Large surfaces may not look round enough.
options.formula: Each step adds a fixed radius.

options.label: Geometric
options.why: Each radius step multiplies the base, so large corners grow quickly.
options.when_to_choose: Choose this if cards are much rounder than inputs.
trade_offs: The steps are harder to remember.
options.formula: Each step multiplies the base radius.
